proseChanges.summary: **Release identity on health:** `/health` now includes `release: {version, sourceCommit}` on both healthy and unavailable responses, baked into the Worker at build time. Managed source copies use the upstream release commit recorded in `rer-upstream.json`; publisher checkouts use Git HEAD. An archive without provenance or its own Git history reports a null source commit, and malformed upstream provenance refuses the build. The existing deployment identity `{sourceSha, fingerprint, versionId}` and deployment health comparison remain unchanged. Release identity alone does not prove healthy storage or provider readiness. **Original installation owner recovery:** a compatible Managed installation can recover only its unambiguous original installation owner, with current platform custody and a verified, installation-scoped platform assertion after recovery-passkey proof. A remembered platform session or email alone is insufficient. Independently controlled installations retain the native-password plus one-time installation-key route under the same first-owner restriction. Both routes require proving a replacement authenticator or passkey before any new session; a newly registered passkey must also prove possession. Completion replaces factors and recovery codes, revokes old sessions and outstanding sign-in/reset links, and retains memberships and roles. Ambiguous older owner anchors require separately authorized binding; lost native and platform proof has no automatic bypass. **Shared-account recovery:** a fresh native password or emailed sign-in proof starts a request, then one current, recently factor-confirmed owner of every affected workspace must consent. Installation custody and platform roles cannot supply that consent; the installation first owner and platform administrators cannot use this generic route. Requests expire within 15 minutes, authority changes invalidate stale requests and approvals, and limits and neutral refusals constrain the recovery doors. Recovery audit records contain IDs and fixed reasons, never credentials or recovery secrets. Replacement-factor proof precedes admission here too. **Recovery backup and restore:** portable archives exclude live requests, approvals, nonces, pending factors and capabilities. Restore clears Managed custody acknowledgement and requires fresh recovery and custody binding; spent manual-key history and the durable revocation watermark remain. Keep that watermark on code rollback. Recovery completion and member erasure use the existing guarded authority boundaries. **Fresh hosted installs:** native setup, ordinary support and release identity on health are active after building this release. Managed owner recovery is active only on a compatible Managed install with configured and acknowledged platform custody and the verified platform assertion; installing SQL alone does not enable it. The independent manual route needs its private installation key, and shared-account recovery needs native proof and every affected workspace consent. Legacy import and adoption stay inert until a legacy package is imported through the approved flow; cleanup continues for registered packages. Updating starts no import, sends no mail and grants no historical-user access. Live platform/provider qualification, real-customer remote importer use and signed migration-before-Worker delivery remain separate. **Migrations:** one since v0.4.25: `330_identity_recovery.sql`, for 196 migration files in total. It adds recovery tables, indexes, credential/membership invalidation triggers and the initial authority row; it is additive and does not rewrite existing accounts, factors, memberships or spent-key history. On v0.4.25 or v0.4.24, apply this missing filename once even though 331 and 332 are already recorded. A v0.4.23 installation applies 328, 329, 330, 331 and 332 once in filename order, retaining earlier buyer steps and 332's conditional cleanup of an untouched empty inventory marker. Stop the old Worker and complete missing migrations BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. Migration 326 remains absent. The generated deployment declaration now includes 330; its resource, secret and native-setup declarations otherwise remain as on main.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.25 has 195 migrations, no baked release identity on health and the earlier installation-key recovery flow.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.26 carries build-time release identity, scoped first-owner recovery, all-affected-workspace consent, replacement-factor proof before admission and recovery portability exclusions. Migration 330 brings the inventory to 196 files. Upgrade baselines: v0.4.25, v0.4.24 and v0.4.23; rer remains 0.2.112.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.25 without resetting; v0.4.24 and v0.4.23 are also upgrade baselines. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state, private settings and installation encryption custody, then stop the old Worker. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. On v0.4.25 or v0.4.24, apply 330_identity_recovery.sql once even though 331 and 332 are already recorded. On v0.4.23, apply 328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql, 329_legacy_package_custody.sql, 330_identity_recovery.sql, 331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql and 332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql once in that order. Finish every missing migration BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. Retain earlier published buyer steps, including 332's conditional cleanup; older installations first apply all other missing published migrations in filename order. There is no migration 326. Keep the durable recovery revocation watermark on rollback. Portable restores discard live recovery authority and require fresh Managed custody binding. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. Legacy v1 remains cleanup-only and incomplete cleanup remains pending. No reset, mail activation, recovery adoption, production import, cutover or production deployment is authorized by this preparation.
